scope: Platform resources, configuration, contextual state, execution and authorization. Operational scenarios are applications of these capabilities, not capability names.
availability: Availability is feature-specific. Sandbox is documented as preview and investigation-only in the reviewed guidance. Confirm feature and Region eligibility before configuration.

D15: Learned skills and migration to memory

capabilities.title: Scoped operational workspaces
capabilities.function: An Agent Space binds infrastructure access, integrations and operator access to a configured operational context.
capabilities.resources: Agent Space; resource-investigation role; operator web-app role.
capabilities.operations: Create a space; associate accounts and integrations; configure the separate roles.
capabilities.boundary: Workspace membership does not override the permission policies on connected resources.

capabilities.title: Selected external-tool access
capabilities.function: Account-level MCP providers expose tools that are explicitly associated with individual Agent Spaces.
capabilities.resources: Capability provider; authentication configuration; Agent Space association; selected tools.
capabilities.operations: Register and authenticate a provider; associate it; select tools; update supported connection settings.
capabilities.boundary: Streamable HTTP transport, network reachability, authentication, selected tools and action classification are separate concerns.

capabilities.title: Private integration connectivity
capabilities.function: Private connections provide a network path to endpoints hosted inside a VPC.
capabilities.operations: Create a connection in the Agent Space Region; configure endpoint routing and network access.
capabilities.boundary: Cross-Region reachability requires additional customer connectivity. Network access does not grant application authorization.

capabilities.title: Environment knowledge maintenance
capabilities.function: A managed learning agent examines infrastructure, dependencies, pipelines and previous investigations to produce environment-specific knowledge.
capabilities.resources: Managed learning agent; learned knowledge; History and Triggers views.
capabilities.operations: Inspect learning runs and their triggers; inspect the produced knowledge.
capabilities.boundary: Learning schedules are platform-owned. Learned skills are transitioning automatically to memory; consult the current memory representation rather than assuming a separate permanent store.

capabilities.title: Persistent contextual knowledge
capabilities.function: Managed and custom memory stores retain synthesized information that an agent can selectively retrieve across sessions.
capabilities.resources: Memory store; Markdown memory entry; description; immutable versions; active state.
capabilities.operations: Inspect entries and versions; activate or deactivate stores and entries; maintain custom context; attach stores to custom agents.
capabilities.boundary: Context retrieval is not customer-controlled model-weight training. Stored information does not establish that it was used or that a new diagnosis is correct.

capabilities.title: Standing instruction injection
capabilities.function: Global and agent-specific AGENTS.md content is included at the start of applicable sessions.
capabilities.operations: Edit the appropriate Agent definition; save content; start a new session.
capabilities.boundary: Existing sessions retain startup content. Prompt guidance is not a deterministic authorization control.

capabilities.title: Conditional procedural guidance
capabilities.function: Skills supply reusable procedures and supporting material when their descriptions match the work and their agent scope applies.
capabilities.resources: SKILL.md; optional supporting resources; description; agent-type targeting.
capabilities.operations: Create or import a skill; select its scope; revise its description and procedure.
capabilities.boundary: An available skill is not necessarily selected. Procedural instructions, informational memory and always-loaded instructions are distinct.

capabilities.title: Constrained custom-agent definitions
capabilities.function: A custom-agent definition combines a system prompt with selected tools, skills and attached memory stores.
capabilities.resources: Custom agent; prompt; tool selection; skill and store attachments.
capabilities.operations: Create or edit the definition; use Chat to configure tools; attach only required stores.
capabilities.boundary: New custom agents have no memory attachments. Attached managed stores are read-only to the custom agent; attached custom stores can support writes.

capabilities.title: Explicit invocation and scheduling
capabilities.function: Built-in investigations and custom-agent invocations expose different initiation paths.
capabilities.resources: Investigation; webhook or connected incident system; custom-agent trigger; invocation.
capabilities.operations: Start an investigation manually or through supported incident integration; run a custom agent on demand or on a schedule.
capabilities.boundary: Do not describe built-in incident triggers and custom-agent schedules as one interchangeable event framework.

capabilities.title: Investigation-local computation
capabilities.function: Sandbox supplies an ephemeral Linux execution environment with configurable dependencies and outbound access rules.
capabilities.resources: Agent Space Sandbox settings; package configuration; network allowlist.
capabilities.operations: Opt in; configure permitted packages and outbound endpoints; inspect a controlled investigation execution.
capabilities.boundary: The reviewed preview guidance limits this execution surface to investigations. It is not durable memory or a general deployment runner.

capabilities.title: Authorized state-changing actions
capabilities.function: Directed actions allow eligible mutations only after separate enablement, access configuration and specific approval.
capabilities.resources: Agent Space setting; account elevated role; tool classification; approval record.
capabilities.operations: Enable the feature; configure eligible accounts and tools; review, adjust, approve or reject a proposed operation.
capabilities.boundary: A mitigation recommendation is not permission to execute it. A configured elevated role is a permission ceiling, not standing approval.

capabilities.title: Configuration resources and execution evidence
capabilities.function: Asset APIs manage supported configuration resources; invocation trajectories expose tool calls and outputs for inspection.
capabilities.resources: Asset records and identifiers; custom-agent invocation trajectory.
capabilities.operations: Manage supported assets programmatically; inspect a run and its outputs.
capabilities.boundary: Use asset identifiers where required by the API. A recorded trajectory is evidence of execution, not independent verification of the conclusion.

mechanisms.title: Recurring-monitor knowledge production
mechanisms.trigger: Recent investigations within the Agent Space.
mechanisms.operation: The monitors store groups recurring cause history by alarm or metric. The documented daily learning process runs when there are investigations within the preceding two weeks; it retains per-investigation evidence.
mechanisms.state: Entries without updates for two weeks are removed; capacity pressure removes the oldest item. This store is bounded operational context, not an incident archive.
enablement: Confirm the Agent Space has completed investigations and inspect the managed learning agent History.
Open Knowledge → Memories and inspect the monitors store and matching entry.
Confirm the store and entry are active; monitor memory is documented as enabled by default.
mechanisms.controls: Keep current telemetry authoritative when it contradicts historical patterns. Learning runs and data retention are not a model-training control.
mechanisms.verification: Proposed check: retain an earlier verified cause, inspect the resulting entry, then examine a later incident with a different cause but similar symptom. Distinguish entry existence, observable retrieval and diagnosis correctness.

mechanisms.title: Corrective-feedback reflections
mechanisms.trigger: An operator supplies corrective feedback on a completed investigation.
mechanisms.operation: The documented reflections store records lessons about a missed or incorrect cause. Feedback submission and recurring-monitor synthesis are different production paths.
mechanisms.state: Feedback can be updated; the latest submission replaces prior feedback for that investigation. Do not assume that every downstream state is immediately refreshed.
enablement: Open the completed investigation and choose Add feedback, or provide the correction through Chat.
Record the verdict and actual cause; inspect the relevant memory under Knowledge → Memories.
Treat the separate opt-in to share feedback with AWS as a distinct decision.
mechanisms.controls: Use a verified correction, not a convenient hypothesis. AWS sharing requires explicit confirmation; local feedback and external sharing are not the same operation.
mechanisms.verification: Proposed check: link the correction to the original evidence, inspect the stored lesson, and challenge the next diagnosis using current contradictory evidence. Without visible access evidence, report recall as unverified.

mechanisms.title: Selective retrieval and store attachment
mechanisms.trigger: An agent session needs contextual information relevant to its task.
mechanisms.operation: The documented retrieval sequence exposes descriptions before full content. For custom agents, store attachments constrain the accessible collection; new agents start without attachments.
mechanisms.state: Updates create immutable entry versions. Deactivating a store or entry removes it from active access without deleting it.
enablement: Write specific descriptions stating the store subject and relevant situations.
Edit the custom agent and attach only required stores; inspect the resulting definition.
Use supported controls to deactivate stale entries and examine previous versions.
mechanisms.controls: A custom agent can write to attached custom stores; attached managed stores remain read-only. Retrieval internals beyond the documented description-selection process are not asserted.
mechanisms.verification: Proposed check: compare an agent with and without a non-sensitive test-store attachment. Inspect observable reads and verify the answer independently. A repeated phrase alone does not prove retrieval.

mechanisms.title: Startup instruction injection
mechanisms.trigger: A new applicable agent session starts.
mechanisms.operation: The service retrieves applicable AGENTS.md content at startup rather than letting the agent select it by relevance.
mechanisms.state: Saved changes apply to new sessions; already-running sessions keep their startup content.
enablement: Open Agents → Managed agents and select the relevant agent.
On Agent definition, edit Global instructions or that agent's own instructions.
Save and start a new session to assess the change.
mechanisms.controls: Global changes affect all applicable managed agents. Instructions guide behavior but do not expand or restrict IAM authorization by themselves.
mechanisms.verification: Proposed check: use a harmless output-format instruction, compare a pre-existing session with a new one, and record the content revision used. Treat compliance as observed behavior, not guaranteed policy enforcement.

mechanisms.title: Description-based skill selection
mechanisms.trigger: The current task matches a skill description and agent-type scope.
mechanisms.operation: Skills supply procedural instructions through SKILL.md and optional supporting resources. They are selected on demand rather than unconditionally injected like standing instructions.
mechanisms.state: Description, procedure and scope are separate configuration fields that should be maintained together.
enablement: Open Knowledge → Skills and add or import the procedure.
Write a description defining when it applies and select the relevant agent types.
Verify available tools separately; a procedure cannot grant missing tool permissions.
mechanisms.controls: An enabled skill can remain unused when its description or scope does not match. A skill is not an authorization boundary.
mechanisms.verification: Proposed check: submit one matching and one nonmatching task. Inspect available invocation evidence for selection instead of inferring it solely from answer wording.

mechanisms.title: Tool association and directed-action authorization
mechanisms.trigger: The agent selects an associated external tool or proposes an eligible AWS-resource mutation.
mechanisms.operation: MCP registration, authentication, Agent Space association and selected tools establish availability. Mutating operations additionally require directed-action controls. AWS actions use the configured elevated role and approval scoped to the operation and resource.
mechanisms.state: Provider configuration, selected tools, role policies and approvals are different records. Approval is not reusable for a different operation or resource.
enablement: Register and authenticate the provider, associate it with the Agent Space, and select the required tools.
Review tool classifications explicitly. Programmatically registered tools without classification are documented to default to READ_ONLY.
For eligible mutations, enable directed actions and configure the account role or integration; review the exact operation before approval.
mechanisms.controls: Misclassifying a mutating server tool as read-only is an operational hazard. Destructive third-party tools are a separate non-invocable class. A network path does not grant application access.
mechanisms.verification: Proposed check: in an authorized test environment, verify a read, a rejected mutation and one narrowly approved mutation. Retain tool parameters, approval identity and independent resource state before and after.

mechanisms.title: Ephemeral sandbox execution
mechanisms.trigger: An investigation uses the explicitly enabled Sandbox capability.
mechanisms.operation: The platform provides investigation-local computation with preconfigured packages and outbound endpoint rules. This execution surface is separate from directed-action authorization.
mechanisms.state: The environment is ephemeral and scoped to an investigation; do not use it as a persistent knowledge store.
enablement: Open Capabilities → Sandbox → Configure for the Agent Space.
Opt in and set package requirements and permitted outbound hosts, methods and paths.
Confirm current feature and Region availability before an authorized test investigation.
mechanisms.controls: The reviewed preview scope is investigations, not all chat or custom-agent work. Network permissions and workload permissions remain separate controls.
mechanisms.verification: Proposed check: run a harmless computation, confirm allowed and denied outbound requests, and verify that the output is retained in investigation evidence rather than assumed to persist in the runtime.

exercise.title: Verify contextual recall without accepting a stale diagnosis
exercise.label: Proposed prepared-result exercise; no live execution or runtime guarantee
steps: Inspect a completed investigation and its verified correction.
Inspect the monitor entry or reflection and its current state.
Review a later invocation for observable retrieval evidence.
Challenge the conclusion with current contradictory telemetry and record unknowns.
exercise.acceptance: Report three separate outcomes: memory exists, memory use is observable or unverified, and diagnosis is independently supported or rejected.
